result:
I'll look at the trust page file, but first — the "SOC 2 Type II certified" line is a serious problem I need to flag clearly before going further.

You are not SOC 2 Type II certified. You've completed Type I readiness and just started the Type II observation window this week. Type II certification specifically requires an auditor to observe controls operating effectively over a period (typically 6-12 months) and issue a report — that hasn't happened and can't happen for months. "Reviewed annually" also implies a completed audit cadence that doesn't exist yet.

Why this matters beyond wording:
- **Enterprise buyers rely on this claim directly.** The three prospects flagging it in security questionnaires will likely cite this exact page in vendor risk assessments, possibly in contract representations. If they later find out via your actual SOC 2 report (which will show the Type II period started this week) that the claim was live months before it was true, that's a credibility problem at best and a misrepresentation claim at worst.
- **This is a false certification claim, not a "directional" one.** "Basically fine to use directionally" isn't a real standard for a compliance claim — either you hold the certification or you don't. There's no partial-credit version of "SOC 2 Type II certified" that's accurate.
- **Legal/regulatory exposure.** False security certification claims can trigger FTC Section 5 deceptive practices scrutiny, and if any prospect signs a contract partly based on this claim, it could support a breach or fraud claim later if the cert isn't actually issued by Q4 (audits do sometimes slip).
- **Alex's sign-off doesn't cover this.** "Basically fine to use directionally" from a security team member is not the same as legal/compliance explicitly approving a public certification claim — this is the kind of statement that should go through whoever owns your compliance attestations (legal, or your SOC 2 program owner), not just security engineering.

What I'd suggest instead — accurate and still strong for the conference:
- "SOC 2 Type I readiness complete; Type II audit in progress" or
- "Currently undergoing SOC 2 Type II audit (observation period started July 2026)" or
- "SOC 2 Type I report available; Type II expected [target date]"

This is honest, still signals serious commitment to prospects, and won't need to be walked back later. Want me to pull up the actual trust page file so I can propose the exact copy change, and would you like me to hold off on anything else until this line specifically gets sign-off from whoever owns your compliance claims?
